folkways.ponder.book_modes.header: One book, three things a click can mean
folkways.ponder.book_modes.text_1: A left click with a bound book acts on the world. Which of three things it does shows on the book itself.
folkways.ponder.book_modes.text_2: Pointing: a left click takes the block or the body under your crosshair into the colony, or back out of it.
folkways.ponder.book_modes.text_3: Sneak and scroll turns the book to the next gesture. A second book keeps whatever it was left in.
folkways.ponder.book_modes.text_4: Marking out: that same click draws a box instead, one click on each of two opposite corners.
folkways.ponder.book_modes.text_5: Hold Ctrl (Cmd on a Mac) and scroll. Before the box is framed this sets a reach, and a Ctrl click drops a corner that far out, in open air. Once it is framed, it pushes the face you aim at in or out.
folkways.ponder.book_modes.text_6: Then right click. The panel asks what the ground is for, and the answers come from the parts of Folkways you have installed: a farm, a pasture, a building, and so on.
folkways.ponder.book_modes.text_7: Drawing a line: each left click adds a stop, joined to the one before, up to 4096 of them. A right click asks what the path is for.
folkways.ponder.book_modes.text_8: Sneak and left click throws the box or line you are drawing away.
folkways.ponder.book_modes.text_9: Aimed at a zone or path already marked out, right click opens its settings, whichever gesture the book is in. Anywhere else, it opens the colony panel.
folkways.ponder.building.header: Building: draw it, and the colony raises it
folkways.ponder.building.text_1: With the book marking out, frame the ground and pick Raise a building from what the box can become. A line drawn with the book offers it too.
folkways.ponder.building.text_2: Then choose a pattern and its few settings, down to the blocks it is made of. Folkways ships a few, data packs add more under folkways/pattern, and your own go in the folkways/pattern folder of your game.
folkways.ponder.building.text_3: Residents with the building trade take the order. First they clear what stands where the drawing wants empty space, working down from the top.
folkways.ponder.building.text_4: Then they lay it from the bottom up, a cell at a time, with blocks fetched from the colony's stores.
folkways.ponder.building.text_5: While you hold the book, the blocks still to go show as ghosts, and a card over the site counts the cells laid and lists, under Still needs, what the rest will take.
folkways.ponder.building.text_6: A cell with nowhere in reach to stand gets a column of scaffolding beside it, taken from the stores. Once that part is laid it comes down, and the scaffolding goes back.
folkways.ponder.building.text_7: The Building page lists every build order with its cells done out of the total. Deleting one stops the work and takes any scaffolding it put up back down.
folkways.ponder.building.text_8: A pattern such as the mine grows in rounds: once one round is built, the next is drawn onto what stands now. The page says which round is coming up.
folkways.ponder.building.text_9: In creative mode, a drawing you confirm stands up at once.
folkways.ponder.colony_book.header: A colony is the blocks you mark
folkways.ponder.colony_book.text_1: An empty colony book is crafted from a plain book. It belongs to no colony yet.
folkways.ponder.colony_book.text_2: A right click opens the colony panel. With the empty book in your main hand it offers one button, New Colony. Press it, and the book is the new colony's deed.
folkways.ponder.colony_book.text_3: Craft that book together with a blank one to get a second deed for the same colony.
folkways.ponder.colony_book.text_4: Left click a chest with the bound book and it joins the colony as storage. Click it again to take it back out.
folkways.ponder.colony_book.text_5: Besides containers, only blocks some part of Folkways puts to use can join: a work station, a bed. What each is for is shown where it is used.
folkways.ponder.colony_book.text_6: Anything else is refused: the colony has no use for it.
folkways.ponder.colony_book.text_7: Bodies take the same click. Pointed at one of your own residents, it lets them go.
folkways.ponder.colony_book.text_8: A colony is not a patch of ground you fence off. It is the blocks you marked yourself.
folkways.ponder.colony_panel.text_1: A right click with the bound book opens the colony panel. Its pages are listed down the left side, in three groups.
folkways.ponder.colony_panel.text_2: Under Colony come its own pages. Workforce sets each resident's work priorities, and Storage lists what the colony's containers hold.
folkways.ponder.colony_panel.text_3: Storage lists every item held in the colony's containers, with how many. Refresh counts again.
folkways.ponder.colony_panel.text_4: At the foot of Settings, Delete colony ends the colony for good. It only goes through once you type out the phrase it asks for.
folkways.ponder.colony_panel.text_5: Under Production, every installed part of Folkways adds a page: Workshop for the stations, Household for the beds, and so on. Their own lists live there, like the fuel stations may burn and the food residents may eat.
folkways.ponder.colony_panel.text_6: Under Preferences, Settings holds the colony's Tools list. Residents only take up tools on it, and an empty list allows none. It starts out with every tool some work asks for.
folkways.ponder.colony_panel.text_7: Lessons holds a folder for every installed part of Folkways. Open one to watch a single lesson, or all of them in a row.
folkways.ponder.colony_panel.text_8: Anywhere in the panel, hover a page's tab and hold the ponder key to play the lesson for that page.
folkways.ponder.create_handoff.header: Handing a Create schematic to the colony
folkways.ponder.create_handoff.text_1: With Create installed, a schematic you have put in place with Create's own tools can go to the colony instead of to a schematicannon.
folkways.ponder.create_handoff.text_2: Hold the schematic, and the colony's book in your other hand.
folkways.ponder.create_handoff.text_3: The schematic's tools have one more among them: Hand Off, marked with the colony book. Choose it and right click.
folkways.ponder.create_handoff.text_4: A small window asks one thing: what to do with cells the blueprint leaves empty. Leave what stands there, which it starts on, or dig it out.
folkways.ponder.create_handoff.text_5: Place the build order. It is filed where the schematic stands, turned and mirrored the way you set it.
folkways.ponder.create_handoff.text_6: From there it is a build order like any other: residents raise it, and it shows on the Building page. It is never raised at once, not even in creative.
folkways.ponder.dispatch.header: Dispatch: order from a Create package network
folkways.ponder.dispatch.text_1: A package network built with Create: stock behind a packager and a stock link, and a Stock Ticker to order from. The colony only takes on a network where every packager hands its parcels only to frogports beside it, and all those frogports hang on one chain net, turning and in one dimension. Should that stop being so, the colony orders nothing until it is put right. Let nothing else take from those packagers, or orders go astray.
folkways.ponder.dispatch.text_2: With the book pointing, left-click any piece of the network: a linked block, a packager, a chain conveyor or a frogport on its chains. The colony takes the whole network on; the same click gives it back.
folkways.ponder.dispatch.text_3: A network locked in Create can only be handed over by someone allowed to run it.
folkways.ponder.dispatch.text_4: A Stock Ticker is a desk. A resident with the Dispatch trade sits on a seat beside it, on the same level or one below, and keeps it.
folkways.ponder.dispatch.text_5: The colony only orders from a network with its own keeper at the desk. With nobody there, the stock is counted but out of reach.
folkways.ponder.dispatch.text_6: Every Package Frogport along the network's chains is a pick-up point, except the ones beside its packagers, where parcels set out. The colony sends to whichever point is handiest. A point whose address is exactly * or contains any of { } , \ is never used by the colony on its own.
folkways.ponder.dispatch.text_7: When the colony needs goods the network has in stock, it sends for them to a pick-up point. A hauler waits for the parcels and takes out what was ordered.
folkways.ponder.dispatch.text_8: Parcels nobody here is waiting for are emptied as well, so strays do not fill the pick-up point.
folkways.ponder.dispatch.text_9: The Dispatch page lists the networks taken on, whether someone is at the desk, each pick-up point, and what is on the way.
folkways.ponder.farming.header: Farming: draw a plot, and let it come back
folkways.ponder.farming.text_1: With the book marking out, click two opposite corners to frame a plot. What it grows is the one setting on it: wheat here.
folkways.ponder.farming.text_2: Residents hoe the ground inside the box. A hoe is the one tool a plot asks for, and the Tools list under Settings has to allow it: an empty list allows none.
folkways.ponder.farming.text_3: Then they sow it, and come back when the crop is ripe. Crops that don't need farmland, like cane or saplings, are sown without hoeing.
folkways.ponder.farming.text_4: Most crops leave the soil bare once harvested, and the next round is sown on the same ground.
folkways.ponder.farming.text_5: Sugar cane is cut once it stands three tall, bamboo at four, and only down to the bottom stalk. What stays keeps growing on its own.
folkways.ponder.farming.text_6: Melons and pumpkins give up the fruit only. The vine is left standing and grows another one.
folkways.ponder.farming.text_7: A wood lot is a plot whose crop is a sapling. The same cycle: every log of the tree is felled, the leaves are left where they are, and a sapling goes back where one has room to grow.
folkways.ponder.farming.text_8: A farmer with the Replanter perk resows as they harvest, using a seed from what the crop just dropped. It only works for crops cut down whole, like wheat, not for cane, fruit or trees.
folkways.ponder.fishing.header: Fishing: frame the bank, not the water
folkways.ponder.fishing.text_1: A fishery frames the bank the residents stand on.
folkways.ponder.fishing.text_2: Never the water itself. Frame the bank, and the water within reach of it is what gets fished.
folkways.ponder.fishing.text_3: Each fishery fishes the one block of water nearest its bank, and two fisheries never share one. If that block is already taken, the second fishery sits idle.
folkways.ponder.fishing.text_4: A rod is the one tool a cast asks for, and it has to be on the Tools list under Settings.
folkways.ponder.fishing.text_5: Then they stand there and wait out the bite. The line running to the float is how you tell fishing apart from idling.
folkways.ponder.fishing.text_6: Practice shortens the wait: the Quick hands perk brings the bite on sooner.
folkways.ponder.golems.header: Golems: put your Modular Golems to work
folkways.ponder.golems.text_1: With the book on pointing, left click a Modular Golem you own. It joins the colony as a resident; click it again and it leaves.
folkways.ponder.golems.text_2: Only the golem's owner can hand it over, and one that already belongs to another colony stays there.
folkways.ponder.golems.text_3: In the colony it drops its own goals and picks no fights, and golem command items do nothing to it. When it leaves, it gets its own ways back.
folkways.ponder.golems.text_4: It works in the trades its body allows: a metal golem hauls and builds, a dog golem only hauls, and a humanoid golem can also craft, drive and dispatch.
folkways.ponder.golems.text_5: It never eats or sleeps. Its knacks are built in, so it does not get better with practice.
folkways.ponder.golems.text_6: Below 60% of its health, a golem carrying something golems are repaired with, such as iron ingots, spends one from its pack to mend itself.
folkways.ponder.household.text_1: A bed joins the colony with the book. Each resident claims a free one as his own, and the Human residents page lists the beds nobody has yet.
folkways.ponder.household.text_2: Walking tires him, and so does standing at work. Tired enough, he goes back to his own bed and sleeps it off. Without a bed of his own he has nowhere to sleep.
folkways.ponder.household.text_3: Work and walking consume food; time spent working and distance walked build fatigue.
folkways.ponder.household.text_4: The colony keeps a couple of meals from the food list in each resident's pack, and he eats when he is hungry. The list is on the Human residents page and starts out with the usual cooked meats, bread and stews.
folkways.ponder.household.text_5: With nothing from the list in store, his pack stays empty. A starving resident loses health.
folkways.ponder.household.text_6: Hold the book, and the card over each resident nearby shows a drumstick for how full he is and a moon for how rested.
folkways.ponder.household.text_7: With nothing to do, a resident wanders over to the nearest neighbour and stands chatting a while, or just loiters about.
folkways.ponder.orders.header: Orders: name what you want kept, the colony works out the rest
folkways.ponder.orders.text_1: An order keeps one item stocked in one container. Open one of the colony's chests, and the Orders page beside it files the draft into that chest.
folkways.ponder.orders.text_2: The draft is an item, a Refill below mark, a Fill to count, and a Priority from -2, served first, to 2, served last.
folkways.ponder.orders.text_3: Maintain files it as a standing order: once the chest drops below the refill mark, it is filled back up to the Fill to count. Deliver fills it to that count once, and the order is done.
folkways.ponder.orders.text_4: You order the finished goods. Fetching the grain and working it at a crafting table, stonecutter or smithing table of the colony's is the colony's business.
folkways.ponder.orders.text_5: What must be smelted goes through a furnace, blast furnace or smoker of the colony's, kept fed from the fuel list on the Workshop page: coal and charcoal, to start with.
folkways.ponder.orders.text_6: Nobody goes out to dig for an order. If the stores hold neither the goods nor what they are made from, it waits.
folkways.ponder.orders.text_7: To withdraw an order, open its chest and press Del beside it on the Orders page.
folkways.ponder.pasture.header: Pastures: say how many head, and the herd holds there
folkways.ponder.pasture.text_1: Frame a pen the way you frame a plot. It has three settings: the animal it keeps (cows, sheep, pigs or chickens), a target head count from 0 to 64, and a shear switch.
folkways.ponder.pasture.text_2: The Pastures page lists every pen: its animal, how many stand in it against the target, and how many of those are grown.
folkways.ponder.pasture.text_3: Below the target, residents feed the grown animals in pairs, and the pairs breed. Young ones count toward the head as soon as they are born.
folkways.ponder.pasture.text_4: Above the target, the whole surplus is culled in one go, always from the grown animals. Six head against a target of four: two cows go. A target of 0 culls every grown one.
folkways.ponder.pasture.text_5: Milk is drawn only when something in the colony asked for milk, and each cow gives it once a day.
folkways.ponder.pasture.text_6: While the shear switch is on, sheep are shorn once their wool is back, and the shears must be on the Tools list under Settings. In a chicken pen, eggs are picked up where they fall.
folkways.ponder.pasture.text_7: Nothing checks the fence for you. A beast that walks off the ground you framed stops being counted, and the pen breeds back up to the target.
folkways.ponder.rail.header: Rail: give the colony a train to run
folkways.ponder.rail.text_1: Build and assemble a train with Create as usual. The colony can run it for you.
folkways.ponder.rail.text_2: With the colony book in your off hand, use a Train Schedule on the driver's seat of a train that has none. The train takes the schedule, and the colony takes the train on.
folkways.ponder.rail.text_3: An empty hand on the same seat, book still in the off hand, takes the schedule out and gives the train back.
folkways.ponder.rail.text_4: While the train stands at a station with its driver's seat empty, a resident with the Drive trade walks over and sits in it.
folkways.ponder.rail.text_5: Add Driver Seated to the stop's wait conditions, and the train waits there until every driver sent for has sat down.
folkways.ponder.rail.text_6: With a driver aboard, a train that calls at two or more stations and has a free seat is a way to get about. Residents on their way somewhere ride it from one of its stations to another.
folkways.ponder.rail.text_7: Add All Residents Alighted to a stop, and the train holds there until everyone getting off at that station is off.
folkways.ponder.rail.text_8: The Rail page lists each train taken on, its stations, whether it is running or at a stop, and when it has no driver.
folkways.ponder.residents.header: Residents: who comes, what they take on, how they look
folkways.ponder.residents.text_1: A newcomer needs room: a free bed joined with the book, and stored food for every resident plus one more mouth.
folkways.ponder.residents.text_2: Someone must also be waiting. Newcomers gather over time, more slowly as the colony grows, and only a few wait at once. Let one in on the Human residents page brings the next, unless the server has switched arrivals off.
folkways.ponder.residents.text_3: On the Workforce tab each resident has a cell per trade: click it to allow or forbid that trade, scroll it to rank it 1 to 4. You rank trades, never tasks, and a forbidden trade is never handed to him.
folkways.ponder.residents.text_4: Work in a trade levels a resident up in it, and each level draws a perk for that trade: quicker hands, more ground per trip, a seed put back as he cuts. The same work draws general ones too, like a brisker walk or a bigger pack.
folkways.ponder.residents.text_5: A newcomer's name and look are drawn from this colony's name pool and look pool. Either pool can be edited entry by entry, or replaced whole by a set a data pack offers. After that, a resident's own window changes his name, surname and look one by one.
folkways.ponder.residents.text_6: Struck by a mob or a player, or caught by fire, a resident drops what he is at and runs away from it.
folkways.ponder.residents.text_7: Pointing the book at one of your residents strikes him off the roster. If one dies, everyone carrying the colony's book is told.
folkways.ponder.workshop.header: The workshop: stations the colony works
folkways.ponder.workshop.text_1: Point the book at a crafting table, a stonecutter or a smithing table and it joins the colony as a station. A furnace, blast furnace or smoker joins the same way.
folkways.ponder.workshop.text_2: A station needs a spot within reach and in sight of it for a resident to stand on. One walled in on every side is left out.
folkways.ponder.workshop.text_3: Residents with the crafting trade work them. They make what the colony's orders call for, and fetch the ingredients from its stores first.
folkways.ponder.workshop.text_4: The stonecutter works its own recipes. The smithing table is used for upgrades only, never for trims.
folkways.ponder.workshop.text_5: At a furnace they put in a load and come back for it once it is cooked. A large batch is shared out among the idle furnaces of the same kind.
folkways.ponder.workshop.text_6: A loaded furnace that has gone cold gets fuel one piece at a time, and only what is on the fuel list: coal and charcoal to begin with.
folkways.ponder.workshop.text_7: Anything left finished in a furnace that nobody is waiting on gets taken out too, so the next load has room.
folkways.ponder.workshop.text_8: The Workshop page counts the stations and lists each one, a furnace with the fuel in it or No fuel. The fuel list is the first row there.
